hero.sub: For your company: CRM, support, AI agents, automations, robots, projects and links. For you: docs, notes, scheduling and a whiteboard. The core of each one is open source and runs on your server for $0.

meta.title: Link: short links on your domain, with analytics
meta.description: Short links with custom domains, cookie-less analytics, QR codes, link-in-bio, Bitly import, an API and webhooks. An open-source Bitly alternative.

hero.sub: Shorten links on your own domain, download the QR code and see clicks by country, referrer and device. Bring your Bitly account with a token or a CSV.

f1.d: go.yourcompany.com/slug. Add the DNS record and verify it; on zerosoft Cloud HTTPS is automatic. Each domain has its own slugs, and you choose where the root goes.

f2.d: Clicks by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. 7, 30 or 90 days or all time, compared with the previous period. No cookies, no fingerprinting.

f3.d: Every link has a QR code in SVG or PNG. Change the destination and the printed code still works.

f4.d: Protect a link with a password, give it an expiry date or a click cap. Once it is reached, the link stops redirecting.

f5.d: Paste a Bitly API token to bring the whole account, or upload the CSV export. Back-halves stay. Verify your domain here first and old links keep working when you move the DNS.

f6.d: One page at zerosoft.ai/@you. Pick your links, put them in order and share it. Clicks are still counted.

f7.d: Tag links by campaign, client or channel. Build UTM URLs without a spreadsheet. Find anything in seconds.

f8.d: Create and measure links from your code with REST API v1. Get link.created and link.clicked as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Your links as CSV and each link’s click log as CSV. You can also read everything through the API.

compare.note: Bitly Core costs $35 a month: $420 a year. Plans with more links and users cost more. Link on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I bring my links from Bitly?
f1.a: Paste a Bitly API token to import the account, or upload the CSV Bitly exports (up to 2,000 links per run). Back-halves are kept. Verify your domain here before you move the DNS and the old links keep working.

f2.q: Do links expire?
f2.a: Only if you give them an expiry date or a click cap. QR codes point at the short link, so you can change the destination without reprinting them.

f3.q: What does it record for each click?
f3.a: Country, referrer, device, browser and operating system, without cookies. Each link’s click log can be filtered by country and exported to CSV.

f4.q: Is there an API?
f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 creates, lists, edits and deletes links and returns their stats. The link.created and link.clicked webhooks are signed with HMAC.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Dub?
f5.a: Lead and sale tracking per click, a partner program, official SDKs, an MCP server and a CLI, one-click DNS setup and link cloaking. Routing by country or device, A/B destinations, QR codes with logo and colors, folder permissions and bulk actions are already in Link.

cta.sub: Paste a URL, pick the alias and share it.

s1.d: One link, or up to 200 at once. Already on Bitly? Import your links through its API or a CSV.

s2.d: Pick the alias, use your own domain, add UTM tags, a QR code, a password, an expiry date or a click limit.

s3.d: Cookie-less analytics by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. Export to CSV or get a webhook on every click.

meta.title: Track: open-source issues, cycles and Gantt
meta.description: Issues with sub-issues, cycles, estimates and list, board, calendar and Gantt views. An open-source Linear alternative.

hero.sub: Issues with sub-issues, relations, priorities and estimates. Plan in cycles and follow the work as a list, board, calendar or Gantt chart.

f1.d: Board, list, calendar and Gantt over the same issues.

f2.d: Group issues into one- or two-week cycles to plan each sprint.

f3.d: Issues with dates show up on a timeline the whole team can read.

f4.d: Break work into sub-issues and mark blockers and duplicates.

f5.d: Mentions, assignments and updates in one place. Mark them read and move on.

f6.d: Custom statuses per team and priorities from low to urgent.

f7.d: Point issues so everyone knows how big the work is before it starts.

f8.d: Filter by status, priority, assignee or cycle. Save the view, open it tomorrow.

f9.d: Every change is logged on the issue. Comment, mention and attach files.

compare.note: Linear Standard costs $8 per user per month. A team of 10 pays $960 a year. Track on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Paste a Linear API key, or upload a CSV export from Linear or Jira, or connect a GitHub repository. You see a preview first; projects, statuses, cycles, milestones, labels and comments come along, and importing again does not duplicate issues.

f2.q: How is work organized?
f2.a: By team, like in Linear. Each team has its own identifier, statuses, members, cycles and saved views, and projects group issues from one or more teams behind one outcome. Issues have a priority, estimate, assignee, dates, sub-issues and relations.

f3.q: Where do I see my work?
f3.a: In My tasks and in the inbox, which collects mentions, assignments and changes to your issues.

f4.q: Does it have an API or webhooks?
f4.a: Not yet. API v1 covers Link, CRM, Cal and Agents. Meanwhile, Flow can create issues when something happens in another app.

f5.q: How do I self-host it?
f5.a: It ships in the same container as the rest of the suite. Issues live in your SQLite file and attachments in the uploads volume.

cta.sub: Create a team, invite people and add this week’s issues.

s1.d: Create a team with your own statuses and invite people to the shared workspace.

s2.d: Issues with sub-issues, relations, priorities and estimates. Group them into cycles to plan each sprint.

s3.d: Follow progress on a list, board, calendar or Gantt timeline. Comments, activity and an inbox keep everyone in sync.

meta.title: CRM: open-source contacts, deals and pipelines
meta.description: Contacts, companies, pipelines, Gmail email sequences, forms, quotes and reports. An open-source HubSpot alternative that runs on your server.

hero.sub: Contacts, companies and deals on a kanban pipeline. It syncs Gmail, sends sequences, captures leads with forms and builds quotes. Your HubSpot export comes in with a preset.

f1.d: Drag deals between stages on a kanban board. As many pipelines as you need, with a probability per stage and a reason for every lost deal.

f2.d: Contacts, companies and deals linked to each other, with company hierarchies, tags, custom fields and duplicate detection.

f3.d: Connect Gmail and every email lands on the contact timeline. Sequences send several steps and stop when someone replies.

f4.d: Calls, meetings, notes and tasks on one timeline per record. Meetings booked in Cal show up on their own.

f5.d: Funnel, forecast, sources, quotas per rep and dashboards with widgets. Reports can be saved.

f6.d: Contacts, companies and deals from any CSV, with column mapping and a preset for the HubSpot export. Export to CSV or JSON.

f7.d: Embeddable forms that create the contact, assign it round-robin and score it with your rules.

f8.d: When a record is created or changes, an email arrives or a quote is accepted: create a task, send an email, call a webhook or enroll in a sequence.

f9.d: A REST API with per-key scopes for contacts, companies, deals, tasks, products and quotes. Signed webhooks when contacts and deals change.

compare.note: HubSpot Sales Hub Professional starts around $50 per user per month. Ten reps pay $6,000 a year before onboarding. CRM on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I bring my data from HubSpot?
f1.a: Connect HubSpot (or Pipedrive) with a read-only token in the importer: contacts, companies, deals, pipelines, owners, custom properties and the activity timeline come over, with a preview first and no duplicates if you run it again. You can also upload CSV exports with the «HubSpot export» preset.

f2.q: Does it send email from my account?
f2.a: Yes, from your connected Gmail, with templates, open and click tracking, and sequences. Sequence steps go out within the hour they are due. On your own server, connecting Gmail needs your own Google OAuth client.

f3.q: Can I limit what each rep sees?
f3.a: Yes. You choose whether members see every record, only their own, or their sales team’s. The rule also applies to search, reports, exports and the API.

f4.q: Is there an API?
f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 covers contacts, companies, deals, activities, tasks, pipelines, products, quotes, associations, tags and forms. Each key has scopes (crm:read, crm:write) and acts with the permissions of whoever created it.

f5.q: What is missing compared to HubSpot?
f5.a: Quotes have no e-signature or payment collection. Forms have no multi-step pages, conditional fields or file uploads. On phones, tables scroll sideways instead of switching to cards.

cta.title2: With the data you already have.
cta.sub: Import a CSV from HubSpot or a spreadsheet and start moving deals.

s1.d: Import contacts and companies from any CSV, mapping each column to a field, with duplicates detected for you.

s2.d: Move deals across the stages of one or several pipelines on a kanban board. Log calls, notes and tasks on each timeline.

s3.d: Workflows send emails, create tasks or call webhooks when something changes. Reports and dashboards show where the money is.

meta.title: Cal: booking pages with Google Calendar
meta.description: Booking pages synced with Google Calendar and Meet, round-robin, routing forms, embeds, an API and webhooks. An open-source Calendly alternative.

hero.sub: Share a link, the other person picks a time and the meeting lands in your Google Calendar with a Meet link. Reminders, rescheduling and cancellation included.

f1.d: One link per meeting: zerosoft.ai/book/you/30min. Days with nothing free are disabled. On desktop, calendar and slots side by side.

f2.d: Busy in Google means busy here. Every booking lands in your calendar, with a Google Meet link when there is no other location. Reschedule or cancel and it updates.

f3.d: Guests see their time zone and you see yours. Buffers before and after, minimum notice and custom questions.

f4.d: Ask a few questions, send each person to the right event type, spread bookings across the team. Each host connects their own Google Calendar.

f5.d: They cancel or reschedule from the link in the email, without creating an account.

f6.d: Confirmation, reschedule and cancellation emails carry an .ics invite. A reminder goes out 24 hours before, with the link to manage the booking.

f7.d: Inline on any page (the height adjusts itself) or behind a popup button.

f8.d: REST API v1 for event types and bookings: list, create, get, cancel. booking.created, booking.rescheduled and booking.cancelled as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Availability is per person across all your event types, so two guests cannot take the same slot. You can also block holidays or focus time.

compare.note: Calendly Standard costs about $12 per user per month. Ten people pay $1,440 a year. Cal on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I move over from Calendly?
f1.a: Paste a Calendly personal access token in Cal settings, under Import from Calendly. Event types (duration, locations and questions) and availability schedules come over, and upcoming bookings too if you choose. Then connect Google Calendar and replace the link or embed on your site.

f2.q: Which calendars does it sync with?
f2.a: Google Calendar: busy times block slots and every booking creates the event with a Meet link. Outlook and iCloud are not supported yet. On your own server, the Google connection needs your own OAuth client.

f3.q: Does it work for a team?
f3.a: Yes. An event type can have several hosts and assigns the booking round-robin to whoever is free. Routing forms send each person to the right event type.

f4.q: Is there an API?
f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 lists event types and creates, lists and cancels bookings with the same rules as the public page. The booking.created, booking.rescheduled and booking.cancelled webhooks are signed.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Calendly?
f5.a: Group or collective events, SMS reminders and Outlook or iCloud calendars. Stripe payments, email workflows and reusable schedules are already in Cal.

cta.sub: Create an event type, connect Google Calendar and send the link.

s1.d: Set the duration, the questions you need answered, your weekly availability, buffers and minimum notice.

s2.d: Send your booking link or embed it on your site, inline or as a popup. Round-robin spreads meetings across the team.

s3.d: The meeting lands in Google Calendar with a Meet link. Everyone gets the invite and a 24h reminder; guests can reschedule or cancel on their own.

meta.title: Docs: a wiki and documents with a block editor
meta.description: Nested pages, a block editor with a / menu, links between pages, mentions, comments and templates. An open-source Notion alternative.

hero.sub: A wiki for your team: nested pages, a block editor with a / menu, page links with [[, @mentions and comments on any block.

f1.d: Paragraphs, headings, lists, to-dos, quotes, code blocks and tables. Type '/' and keep writing.

f2.d: Organize pages in a tree and drag them to nest one under another.

f3.d: Type [[ to link another page and @ to mention someone in the workspace.

f4.d: Comment on the whole page or on one block. Threads can be resolved and reopened.

f5.d: Invite the whole company. Seats are not billed, on your server or on zerosoft Cloud.

f6.d: Every page is stored as JSON in your database. If you self-host, it sits in your SQLite file.

f7.d: Find pages from ⌘K, alongside contacts, links and tasks.

f8.d: Start from meeting notes, a project spec or a weekly retro.

f9.d: Moving a page to the trash takes its subpages with it, and restoring brings them all back.

compare.note: Notion Plus costs about $10 per user per month. A team of ten pays $1,200 a year. Docs on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Export your workspace or a page from Notion as Markdown & CSV and upload the .zip in Docs › Import from Notion. Pages keep their tree, images, files and links between pages; each CSV becomes a database, and each row's page becomes the body of that row.

f2.q: Can several people edit at once?
f2.a: Not in real time. If two people edit the same page at the same time, the second one to save gets a warning and chooses between loading the new version or overwriting it. Each page keeps up to 50 versions you can restore.

f3.q: Can I publish a page on the web?
f3.a: Yes. The pages you publish form a public help center at /h/ plus your handle, with collections, search and a vote per article. On zerosoft Cloud there is no custom domain yet. For a single person, share the page as view only.

f4.q: What do databases have?
f4.a: Typed properties (text, number, select, multi-select, status, date, person, checkbox, URL, email, phone, created and edited time), table, board and gallery views with filters, sorting and grouping, and rows that open as pages. Relations, rollups, formulas and calendar or timeline views are not there yet.

f5.q: Does it have a public API?
f5.a: Not yet. API v1 covers Link, CRM, Cal and Agents. If you self-host, pages are stored as JSON in your SQLite database.

cta.sub: Start from a template and nest pages as it grows.

s1.d: Start from a blank page or a template, and nest pages inside pages to build your wiki.

s2.d: Headings, lists, to-dos and more from the slash menu. Link other pages with [[ and leave comments.

s3.d: Leave comments on any block and find any page from ⌘K.

meta.title: Chat: website chat widget and shared inbox
meta.description: A chat widget for your site, a shared inbox, SLAs, assignment rules, canned responses, an AI bot and CSAT. An open-source Intercom alternative.

hero.sub: A chat widget for your site and a shared inbox for the team. Statuses and priorities, SLAs, assignment rules, canned responses, an AI bot and CSAT.

chat.featuresTitleDim: With the whole team in it.

f1.d: One script tag puts the widget on any site. If you identify the visitor, you see their name and email.

f2.d: Every conversation lands in one inbox the whole team works: assign, reply, snooze and resolve. J and K move between them.

f3.d: Open, pending, snoozed and resolved, with priorities from low to urgent.

f4.d: First-response and resolution targets per priority, with a warning before they are breached.

f5.d: Answers from your canned responses and Docs pages, and hands off to a person at high priority. Without AI configured, it matches by keyword.

f6.d: Show an away message with your expected response time when you're off, and measure satisfaction (1–5) when a conversation is resolved.

f7.d: Route conversations to the right teammate automatically and answer in two keystrokes with saved replies.

f8.d: Your visitors with their conversations and notes. If they leave an email, one click adds them to the CRM.

f9.d: Invite your whole support team. Seats are not billed.

compare.note: Intercom starts around $29 per seat per month. A team of ten pays $3,480 a year. Chat on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I add the widget to my site?
f1.a: Create a widget, copy the script tag and paste it before the closing body tag. It works on any site that serves HTML.

f2.q: Does it handle email or WhatsApp?
f2.a: Not yet. Chat has one channel: the website widget.

f3.q: How does the bot work?
f3.a: It answers until someone on your team replies. It uses AI with your canned responses and Docs pages; without AI configured, it matches by keyword. You can turn it off per widget.

f4.q: Does it connect to the CRM?
f4.a: Yes. If the visitor leaves an email, Chat creates the contact in the CRM and logs the conversation on its timeline.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Intercom?
f5.a: Proactive messages, a public API with webhooks, and conversation export. Internal notes with mentions, tags, macros, the help center and reports per agent or by date range are already in Chat.

cta.sub: Create a widget, paste the script on your site and get your first message.

s1.d: Copy one script tag into your site. Visitors get a webchat that respects your office hours.

s2.d: Every conversation lands in a shared inbox, with states, priorities, assignment rules and SLA timers.

s3.d: Canned responses for the usual questions and an AI bot that handles the repeats. CSAT tells you how it went.

meta.title: Groups: open-source WhatsApp team inbox and group manager
meta.description: A shared inbox for WhatsApp chats and groups: assignment, notes, tickets by emoji, SLAs, broadcasts and bulk group management, linked to your CRM. An open-source Periskope alternative.

hero.sub: One inbox for every WhatsApp chat and customer group. Assign, answer, turn messages into tickets and manage hundreds of groups at once, with each group on its CRM record.

groups.featuresTitle: Every customer group in one place.

f1.d: 1:1 chats and groups from several numbers in one list, with filters for unread, unanswered, mine and label.

f2.d: Create groups one by one or from a CSV, add and remove members in many groups, promote admins and reset invite links.

f3.d: React with an emoji from the app or the phone, or use a keyword, and the message becomes a ticket with priority and due time.

f4.d: A chat that waits longer than your limit shows up as overdue. A reply from the phone also counts.

f5.d: One message with variables to many groups, now or scheduled, with messages per minute and status per recipient.

f6.d: Link a group to a company or contact and its latest messages and open tickets show up there.

f7.d: An agent from Agents can answer in a chat, and Flow reacts to messages and tickets or sends a WhatsApp.

f8.d: Use the WhatsApp Cloud API for 1:1 support, or a WAHA or Evolution API gateway by QR to manage groups.

f9.d: J and K to move, R to reply, N for a note, E to close, A to assign and T for a ticket.

compare.note: Periskope Starter lists at $25 per seat per month (monthly billing, Pro is $35). A team of ten pays $3,000 a year. Groups on your server costs $0; you run the WhatsApp gateway or pay Meta for the official API.

f1.q: How does it connect to WhatsApp?
f1.a: Two ways, chosen per number. The official WhatsApp Cloud API from Meta, for 1:1 chats, media and templates. Or a self-hosted WAHA or Evolution API gateway that links your number by QR, which is what allows group management.

f2.q: Is the QR mode safe for my number?
f2.a: It uses an unofficial WhatsApp Web session, and WhatsApp can restrict a number used this way, especially if it adds many strangers or sends a lot of unrequested messages. Groups sends broadcasts at a pace you set and suggests invite links. For 1:1 messaging we recommend the official API.

f3.q: Can I manage groups with the official API?
f3.a: Not in Groups today. The official API covers 1:1 chats; creating groups and managing members goes through the QR gateway.

f4.q: How do tickets work?
f4.a: A ticket comes from a message: by hand, by reacting with the ticket emoji (from Groups or the phone) or when a customer writes one of your keywords. Each one has status, priority, assignee and due times for first response and resolution.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Periskope?
f5.a: Still to come: a native mobile app, voice calls, round-robin assignment and per-label access for members. Periskope also uses AI to tell questions from comments; Groups flags by time without reply.

cta.sub: Connect a number, bring in your groups and start answering from one inbox.

s1.d: Paste your Cloud API credentials or scan the QR from your gateway.

s2.d: Sync the groups the number already has, or create them from a CSV.

s3.d: Assign chats, leave notes, open tickets and link each group to the CRM.

meta.title: Agents: AI agents that use your knowledge
meta.description: AI agents that answer from your own knowledge and use tools across CRM, Cal, Track and Flow. An open-source alternative to Intercom Fin.

hero.sub: AI agents that help your customers using your own knowledge and act across the suite: they save leads, book meetings and hand off to your team when needed.

f1.d: Describe what it does, how it talks and when it uses each tool, the way you would brief a new hire.

f2.d: It searches your Docs pages, up to 20 URLs (each one is read as a single page; it does not crawl the site) and your saved Chat replies.

f3.d: It saves leads to the CRM, offers times and books in Cal, files Track issues and runs flows.

f4.d: When the visitor asks or the agent is unsure, it alerts your team and stops replying.

f5.d: Your site’s Chat widget, a full-screen public page and an API for your own app.

f6.d: Test it before you publish, and every conversation records which tools it used and with what data.

compare.note: Intercom charges about $0.99 for every conversation Fin resolves, on top of Intercom seats. At 1,000 resolutions a month that is $11,880 a year. Agents on your server costs whatever your AI model uses.

f1.q: Which AI model does it use?
f1.a: Any model on the AI Gateway, in provider/model format (for example, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5). On your server you pay usage directly with your key; on zerosoft Cloud it is billed by tokens.

f2.q: Can it make up answers?
f2.a: It answers from your knowledge and hands off to a person when it is unsure. Every reply is logged with the tools it used, so you can review it.

f3.q: Where does it talk to my customers?
f3.a: In the Chat widget on your site, on its own public page and through API v1 (agents:run scope) from your app.

f4.q: Can it change my data?
f4.a: Only through the tools you turn on, and only inside your workspace. To book a meeting it needs a slot it offered itself and the visitor’s confirmation.

f5.q: Can I bring my Fin setup?
f5.a: There is no importer. Paste your instructions as the brief and add your Docs pages and the URLs of your web pages as knowledge.

cta.sub: Create an agent from a template and try it in the playground before you publish it.

s1.d: Pick a template (support, sales or lead qualification) or start blank.

s2.d: Add Docs pages and websites, and turn on only the tools it needs.

s3.d: Connect it to the Chat widget, share its page or call it through the API.

meta.title: Flow: open-source visual automations
meta.description: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any API. An open-source alternative to Zapier and n8n.

hero.sub: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any service with an API. Triggers, conditions, loops and AI steps on one canvas.

f1.d: A Cal booking, a Link click, a new contact, an issue or a Chat message.

f2.d: Start from a POST to a secret URL or every N minutes, in your time zone.

f3.d: Conditions, branches and loops over lists, on a canvas where you drag and connect nodes.

f4.d: Create contacts, enroll in sequences, open issues, reply in Chat and write to Docs.

f5.d: Summarize, classify or draft text in the middle of a flow.

f6.d: Every run keeps what went in and out of each node, so you find the error fast.

compare.note: Zapier Team costs about $103.50 a month billed monthly and includes 2,000 tasks; go past that and the price goes up. Flow on your server does not charge per task.

f1.a: An event in any app (a booking, a click, a new contact, an issue, a chat message), an incoming webhook, a schedule or the Test button.

f2.q: Does it connect to outside services?
f2.a: Yes: through HTTP requests to any public HTTPS API and through incoming webhooks. To post in Slack, its webhook is enough.

f3.q: Can I bring my zaps?
f3.a: There is no importer. Templates cover the most common cases, and building a new flow takes minutes.

f4.q: Is there a run limit?
f4.a: On your server there is no per-task charge. Each workspace has an hourly run cap so a broken loop does not overload the server.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Zapier?
f5.a: The number of integrations. Flow has nodes for Slack, Google Sheets, Gmail, Stripe, Notion, Discord and Telegram; Zapier connects thousands of apps. For the rest, Flow speaks HTTP: if a service has an API or webhooks, you connect it with an HTTP request.

cta.sub: Start from a template and turn on your first flow today.

s1.d: An event in the suite, an incoming webhook or a schedule.

s2.d: Add conditions, loops, HTTP requests, emails and actions from each app.

s3.d: Run a test with real data, check each node’s output and switch it on.

meta.title: Robots: open-source browser automation
meta.description: Robots that browse, fill in forms and extract data for you. An open-source alternative to UiPath.

hero.sub: Browser robots that visit pages, click, fill in forms and extract data for you. Run them by hand, on a schedule or from Flow.

f1.d: Open a URL, click, fill in, wait, extract text or tables and take screenshots.

f2.d: Define named values and the same robot works for another product or another page.

f3.d: It walks through lists of items and decides what to do based on what it finds.

f4.d: It runs every day at the time you choose, or by hand when you need it.

f5.d: A flow starts it, waits for the result and uses the data in the next step.

f6.d: Each run opens a fresh browser and closes it when done. On Vercel, inside a microVM.

compare.note: UiPath Basic starts at about $25 a month for up to 2 robots; Standard and Enterprise are quoted separately. Robots on your server costs $0; on Vercel you pay for the Sandbox minutes you use.

f1.a: A browser that follows steps: open a page, click, fill in fields, read text or tables and take screenshots. You build it step by step, without writing code.

f2.q: Where does it run?
f2.a: On your server with Chromium, or in an isolated Vercel Sandbox microVM if you deploy on Vercel.

f3.q: Does it work on sites with a login?
f3.a: Yes. Store the username and password in Flow Credentials: they are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and the robot uses them without showing them in the logs. It can also keep the session between runs, encrypted. Regular inputs are stored in plain text and the whole workspace can see them, so do not put passwords there.

f4.q: How do I use what it extracts?
f4.a: Every run returns JSON. From Flow you can create contacts, send an email or file an issue with that data.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Browse AI?
f5.a: Picking what to extract by clicking on the page (today you write CSS selectors), prebuilt robots for popular sites, robots generated by AI from a URL, residential proxies by country, captcha handling and self-healing when a site changes its layout.

cta.sub: Start from a template: read a table, track a price, fill in a form or take a screenshot.

s1.d: Start with Go to URL and add clicks, fields and extractions.

s2.d: Run it by hand and see what it extracted at each step.

s3.d: Give it a schedule or call it from a flow.

meta.title: Notes: open-source notes, notebooks and search
meta.description: Notebooks, checklists, a web clipper and questions about your notes. An open-source alternative to Evernote.

hero.sub: Quick notes, notebooks, checklists and full-text search. Save pages with the clipper and ask your notes what you forgot.

f1.d: Organize your way and keep what you use every day at the top.

f2.d: Find a note by any word inside it.

f3.d: Lists to tick off, from groceries to opening the shop.

f4.d: Save any page as a note, with the text you selected and the source link.

f5.d: Answers that come only from your notes, with the sources in view.

f6.d: Share a note with anyone and switch the link off when you are done.

compare.note: Evernote Personal costs about $14.99 a month billed monthly. Notes on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Only you. If you share a note, anyone with the link can read it, and you can switch the link off at any time.

f2.q: How do I save things from the web?
f2.a: With the clipper: drag a button to your bookmarks bar and, from any page, save it as a note with the text you selected.

f3.q: What does Ask your notes do?
f3.a: It answers using only what is in your notes and shows which ones it used. If none mention it, it tells you.

f4.q: Can I use it from the keyboard?
f4.a: Yes. Press N for a new note, and search finds text inside all your notes.

f5.q: Can I import from Evernote?
f5.a: There is no importer yet. You can paste your notes or use the clipper to save web pages.

cta.sub: Press N and start typing. Your notes are yours alone.

meta.title: Board: open-source infinite whiteboard
meta.description: An infinite whiteboard shared with your team, with autosave and read-only links. An open-source alternative to Miro.

hero.sub: An infinite whiteboard to sketch, plan and explain ideas with your team. It saves itself and you share it with a link.

f1.d: Draw, write and arrange ideas without running out of room.

f2.d: Anyone on your team can open the board and edit it.

f3.d: It saves while you work and tells you if someone changed it elsewhere.

f4.d: Spot each board at a glance and use one as a template.

f5.d: Show a board to a client without letting them edit.

f6.d: Paste screenshots and photos next to your notes.

compare.note: Miro Starter costs about $10 per user per month billed monthly. Ten people: $1,200 a year. Board on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Your whole workspace. If you share it by link, everyone else can only view it.

f2.q: Does it save itself?
f2.a: Yes, as you draw. If someone changed it elsewhere, it lets you know and you choose which version to keep.

f3.q: Can I paste images?
f3.a: Yes. Each board has a size limit; if you go over it, shrink or remove some images.

f4.q: What is it built on?
f4.a: Excalidraw, the open-source hand-drawn whiteboard editor.

f5.q: Can I bring my Miro boards?
f5.a: There is no importer. Export the Miro board as an image and paste it into a new board.

cta.sub: Open a new board and share it with your team.

meta.title: Voice: open-source voice dictation and meeting notes
meta.description: Dictate into any zerosoft field and take meeting notes with live transcripts, AI summaries, decisions and tasks. An open-source alternative to Wispr Flow and Granola.

hero.sub: Hold a key, talk and the clean text lands where you were typing. Record a call from your browser, jot a few lines and AI writes the notes with the transcript, in the same suite as your CRM, Docs and Track.

voice.featuresTitleDim: Dictation and meetings in one app.

f1.d: Hold Alt+Space in any zerosoft text field, or double tap it for hands-free. A desktop app to dictate into any program is on the way.

f2.d: Filler words go, punctuation and lists appear and spoken corrections like "Monday, no, Tuesday" are applied, with your dictionary, snippets and a tone per context.

f3.d: Record your microphone, or your microphone and a browser tab with Meet, Zoom or Teams. No extra participant joins the call and the audio is discarded once transcribed.

f4.d: A live transcript split into Me and Them, AI notes built from what you jotted with a template per meeting type, plus decisions and next steps.

f5.d: Next steps become Track issues or CRM tasks, the note goes to Docs or Notes and, linked to a Cal booking, lands on the contact timeline. Ask any meeting what was said.

f6.d: Transcription goes through the provider you configure (Whisper through the AI Gateway, OpenAI, Deepgram or AssemblyAI), with the same quota and usage log as the other apps.

s1.d: Hold a key, talk and see clean text where you were typing.

s2.d: Voice listens to your mic and the call tab and transcribes as you talk, split into Me and Them. With Deepgram or AssemblyAI it also tells speakers apart.

s3.d: The summary, decisions and next steps go to Docs, Notes, Track or the CRM.

compare.note: Wispr Flow Pro costs $12 per user per month billed yearly ($15 monthly) and Granola Business costs $14 per user per month. Together that is $26: a team of ten pays $3,120 a year. List prices checked on October 25, 2026. Voice on your server costs $0 plus whatever your transcription provider charges.

f1.a: Yes, on the web: dictation in every zerosoft field and meeting notes at /app/voice. The workspace needs a transcription provider configured (the AI Gateway, OpenAI, Deepgram or AssemblyAI).

f2.q: Is there a desktop app?
f2.a: It is on the way. Its source code is already in the repository (dictation into any program and system audio for meetings, on Mac and Windows), but there are no signed downloads yet.

f3.q: Where is the audio processed?
f3.a: By the transcription provider your workspace uses. A live recording goes in 20-second parts that are transcribed and discarded; an imported file is deleted from storage once it is transcribed, or after 24 hours if it never was. If you self-host zerosoft, you pick the provider and the key.

f4.q: Does it add a bot to my meetings?
f4.a: No. It records from your browser, the way Granola records from your computer, with no extra participant on the call. Let people know you are transcribing.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Wispr Flow + Granola?
f5.a: The signed desktop and mobile apps, voice commands to rewrite text, calendar reminders from Google or Outlook, folders and share links. The parity table above lists every capability we measure.

cta.sub: Hold Alt+Space in any field, or start a meeting and let Voice write it up.

meta.title: Rec: open-source screen and camera recording
meta.description: Record your screen, your camera or both from the browser, share with a link, get timestamped comments and see who watched. An open-source alternative to Loom.

hero.sub: Record your screen, a window or a tab with your camera in a bubble, right from the browser. When you stop, the link is copied: comments land on the exact second and you see who watched and how much.

f1.d: Screen and camera, screen only or camera only. Drag and resize the camera bubble, pick the microphone, pause and resume.

f2.d: The video uploads in parts while you record, so the link is ready and copied when you finish. Password, expiry and workspace-only access if you want.

f3.d: Comments and emoji reactions pinned to the second, shown on the timeline. One click jumps to that moment.

f4.d: Views, unique viewers, how much each one really watched (skipping ahead does not count), a retention curve, button clicks and the names of signed-in viewers. Export to CSV.

f5.d: Transcript with captions, plus an AI title, summary and chapters you can edit. It needs a transcription provider configured.

f6.d: Trim the start and the end (viewers of a WebM recording get the trimmed copy), add a call to action, pick a thumbnail, embed the player anywhere and organize videos in folders.

s1.d: Pick screen, camera or both, choose the microphone and press start. A 3 second countdown and you are on.

s2.d: When you stop, the link is copied. Paste it in an email, an issue or a chat.

s3.d: Comments on the exact second, reactions and who watched how much.

compare.note: Loom Business costs $15 per user per month billed yearly ($18 monthly); Business + AI costs $20. A team of ten pays $1,800 a year. List prices checked on October 25, 2026. Rec costs $0 on your server plus video storage and, if you want transcripts, the transcription provider.

f1.q: Do I need to install anything?
f1.a: No. Rec records from Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a computer, with no extension. There is no desktop or mobile app yet.

f2.q: Can it record my computer's audio?
f2.a: It records your microphone and, when the browser shares it, the audio of the tab or the screen you pick. Chrome shares tab audio everywhere and system audio on Windows and ChromeOS.

f3.q: Where are videos stored?
f3.a: In your server's file storage (Vercel Blob or a local folder) or in zerosoft Cloud's. If you self-host, videos stay on your infrastructure.

f4.q: Who can watch a video?
f4.a: Anyone with the link, or only signed-in members of your workspace. You can add a password and an expiry date and turn comments on or off. Turning downloads off removes the download button, but a video that streams can still be captured.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Loom?
f5.a: The desktop app, the Chrome extension and mobile apps, drawing on screen, background blur, joining clips, editing by transcript, custom branding and the Slack, Jira and Gmail integrations. The parity table above has the full list.

cta.sub: Open Rec, pick screen, camera or both and record your first video.

meta.title: Talk: open source team messaging, a Slack alternative
meta.description: Public and private channels, direct messages, threads, mentions, search and notifications for your team, in the same suite as your CRM, Track and Docs. Open source alternative to Slack.

hero.sub: Your team's messaging: public and private channels, direct messages and threads, with the same people as your workspace and links to issues, deals and pages that show their status.

talk.featuresTitle: The team's conversations in one place.
talk.featuresTitleDim: Next to your CRM, Track and Docs.

f1.d: Public and private channels by topic, team or customer, with topic, description, members, pins and archiving.

f2.d: One-to-one conversations or groups of up to nine people plus you.

f3.d: Replies in a side panel, with the option to also send them to the channel.

f4.d: @person, @channel, @here and workspace teams, notified in the bell and by email, plus emoji reactions.

f5.d: Unreads and mentions per channel, and search with in:, from:, has: and dates.

f6.d: The same people you already work with in CRM, Track and Docs. A message becomes a Track issue in three clicks.

s1.d: Create a channel per team, project or customer. #general is already there.

s2.d: Workspace people join public channels, or you add them to private ones.

s3.d: Replies, mentions and reactions, with unreads marked and in real time.

compare.note: Slack Pro costs $7.25 per user per month billed annually ($8.75 monthly) and Business+ costs $15. A team of ten pays $870 a year. List prices without promotions, checked on October 25, 2026. Talk on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Open /app/talk: it starts with #general and you can create channels, open direct messages and reply in threads. The parity table shows what is there and what is missing.

f2.q: Does it have calls like Slack huddles?
f2.a: Not yet. Audio and video calls come in a later stage.

f3.q: Will I be able to bring my Slack messages?
f3.a: There is no Slack importer today. If you need one, vote for it on the public board.

f4.q: Does it work with people from other companies?
f4.a: Talk is meant for the people in your workspace. Channels shared with other organizations, like Slack Connect, are not in the initial plan.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Slack?
f5.a: Calls, canvases and lists, marketplace apps, channels shared with other organizations, guests, AI summaries and desktop and mobile apps. The parity table lists it row by row.

cta.title2: Tell us what you are missing.
cta.sub: Try it with your team and vote on the public board for what we should do next.

meta.title: Shop: open-source online store with Stripe and Mercado Pago
meta.description: Sell online with products, variants, stock per location, discount codes, shipping rates and checkout with Stripe or Mercado Pago. An open-source alternative to Shopify and Tiendanube.

hero.sub: Load your catalog or import it from Shopify or Tiendanube, pick a theme and publish. Customers buy as guests with a card, Mercado Pago or a bank transfer, and every order lands in your CRM.

f1.d: Size, color or any option, with a price, SKU, barcode, weight and stock for each combination. Manual or rule-based collections.

f2.d: Stock per location with a history of every change. An order reserves its units and payment takes them out with compare-and-set, so a unit is not sold twice while the order is waiting for payment.

f3.d: Card payments with Stripe Checkout and Mercado Pago Checkout Pro with your own accounts, plus bank transfer. Signed webhooks mark orders paid.

f4.d: Flat or weight rates per country, free over an amount, tax per country and region (added or included) and discount codes with limits and dates.

f5.d: Fulfill with tracking, refund in full or in part, internal notes, a printable packing slip and emails to the customer in the store language.

f6.d: Customers become CRM contacts, Flow reacts to orders and low stock, Link makes campaign links, Agents answers "where is my order?" and the assistant reads your sales.

s1.d: Create products or import the CSV you exported from Shopify or Tiendanube.

s2.d: Paste your Stripe or Mercado Pago keys and add your shipping rates.

s3.d: Pick a theme, upload your logo and share /store/your-store.

compare.note: Shopify’s plans and payment fees are on shopify.com/pricing. Shop costs $0 on your server; Stripe and Mercado Pago charge their usual fees on each sale.

f1.q: Can I move my Shopify or Tiendanube catalog?
f1.a: Yes. Export products as CSV there and import the file in Shop: variants, prices, stock, SEO fields and Shopify photo URLs come along. Orders and customers are not imported.

f2.q: Which payment methods are there?
f2.a: Stripe Checkout (cards and the methods you turn on in Stripe), Mercado Pago Checkout Pro and bank transfer with your own instructions. You use your own accounts and their fees.

f3.q: Do customers need an account?
f3.a: No. Checkout is always as a guest and customers check their order with the order number and their email.

f4.q: Can I use my own domain?
f4.a: Not yet. The store lives at the zerosoft address under /store/your-store.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Shopify?
f5.a: Custom domains, a theme editor, customer accounts, abandoned cart emails, carrier rates and labels, gift cards, returns, point of sale and marketplace channels. The parity table above has the full list.

cta.sub: Open Shop, add your first product and publish your store.

meta.title: Design: open-source graphic design
meta.description: Make social posts, presentations, documents and logos from templates, with your brand kit, comments and export to PNG, JPG and PDF. An open-source alternative to Canva.

hero.sub: Pick a size or a template, change the text, drop in your images and your brand colors, and download it as PNG, JPG or PDF. Your team comments right on the canvas.

f1.d: Instagram post and story, LinkedIn, A4, 16:9 presentation, logo or any size up to 8000 px. 20 templates to start from, and any design can become a workspace template.

f2.d: Text with 12 fonts, shapes, lines, icons, frames and grids. Layers, groups, align and distribute, snapping guides, crop, rotate, lock, undo and keyboard shortcuts.

f3.d: A deck or a carousel in one design. Reorder pages, duplicate them and present them full screen.

f4.d: Logos, colors and fonts for the whole workspace. Admins set them up and everyone applies them from the editor in one click.

f5.d: PNG, transparent PNG, JPG and multi-page PDF at 1x, 2x or 3x. Nothing goes through a server to export.

f6.d: View or edit for the workspace or specific people, a public link you can turn off, comments pinned on the canvas and who has it open.

s1.d: A preset size, a custom one or a template.

s2.d: Change the text, add images and apply your brand colors and fonts.

s3.d: PNG, JPG or PDF, or a link for your team to comment.

compare.note: Canva Business costs $250 per person per year billed yearly ($25 per month billed monthly). A team of ten pays $2,500 a year. Prices checked on October 29, 2026 through public price trackers, since canva.com/pricing did not load from our checker. Design costs $0 on your server plus image storage.

f1.q: Can I bring my Canva designs?
f1.a: There is no importer. Download the Canva design as PNG and use it as an image or a page background.

f2.q: Where are my images stored?
f2.a: In your server file storage (Vercel Blob or a local folder) or in zerosoft Cloud. Uploads go through the same type and size checks as the rest of the suite, up to 4 MB per image (large photos are reduced in the browser).

f3.q: Who can see a design?
f3.a: Only you until you share it. You can give view or edit access to the whole workspace or to specific people, and turn on a view-only public link that you can turn off at any time.

f4.q: Does it have AI?
f4.a: It writes and rewrites text if AI is configured on your server or you use zerosoft Cloud. It does not remove backgrounds or generate images yet.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Canva?
f5.a: Stock photos and graphics, background removal and image generation, video and animation, charts and tables, text effects, uploading your own fonts, SVG export, print-ready PDF, version history and the mobile apps. The parity table above has the full list.

cta.sub: Open Design, choose a template and make your first design.

meta.title: Analytics: open-source product analytics
meta.description: Events from a small JS snippet, trends, funnels, retention, people, dashboards, feature flags and a web analytics overview. An open-source alternative to PostHog.

hero.sub: Paste one script and see who visits, what they click and where they drop off. Trends, funnels and retention on your own events, feature flags with a rollout percentage, and a read-only SQL editor scoped to your project.

f1.d: Page views (single-page apps too), clicks on links and buttons, field changes without their values and form submits. identify, alias and group from code, plus a batch endpoint for your server.

f2.d: Counts and unique users by hour, day, week or month, broken down by any property and compared with the previous period. Funnels of up to 10 steps with a conversion window and the people who dropped.

f3.d: Daily or weekly cohorts by first event and return event. Paths show the most common page sequences per session.

f4.d: Each person with their properties, ids and event timeline. Cohorts by person properties or by how often someone did an event. Admins can delete a person with all their events.

f5.d: On and off flags or variants, a rollout percentage and targeting by person properties. The snippet reads them with isFeatureEnabled and getFeatureFlag.

f6.d: Visitors, page views, sessions, bounce rate, top pages, referrers, countries and devices on one page. For anything else, a read-only SQL editor over your project's events.

s1.d: Each project gets a public key. Limit it to your domains and choose Do Not Track, IP anonymization and retention.

s2.d: Add the script to your site or import it as a module. Events show up in the live stream right away.

s3.d: Build a trend, a funnel or a retention table, save it and pin it to a dashboard.

compare.per: after the first million events a month
compare.note: PostHog charges product analytics by usage: the first million events each month are free and the rest are billed per event, cheaper at higher volumes. We could not verify the current per-event price, so check posthog.com/pricing. Analytics on your server costs $0 plus your database.

f1.a: Create a project, copy the script tag from its setup page and paste it in your site. Or import https://zerosoft.ai/zs.mjs as a module. Servers can post events to /api/ingest/e with the project secret key.

f2.q: Does it record sessions?
f2.a: No. Session replay is not built. Analytics records events and their properties, never the screen.

f3.q: What does autocapture collect?
f3.a: Clicks on links and buttons with their text, which field changed (never what was typed) and form submits. Password fields and anything with the class zs-no-capture are skipped, and text that looks like an email or a long number is dropped.

f4.q: How much traffic can it take?
f4.a: It runs on the same SQLite or Turso database as the rest of zerosoft, so it fits small and mid-size sites: a few million events per project before queries slow down. Funnels, retention and paths read up to 200,000 rows and tell you when they hit that cap.

f5.q: What is missing compared to PostHog?
f5.a: Session replay, heatmaps, the toolbar, experiments, surveys, the data warehouse and pipelines, alerts and server or mobile SDKs. The SQL editor speaks SQLite, not HogQL. The parity table above has the full list.

cta.sub: Open Analytics, create a project and add the snippet to your site.

meta.title: Social: open source social media management, a Hootsuite alternative
meta.description: Schedule posts to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, YouTube, Threads and Bluesky, answer comments and messages from one inbox, approve your team's posts and measure what works. Open source alternative to Hootsuite.

hero.sub: Plan, publish and answer on social media with your team: one composer for every network, a shared calendar, approvals, a unified inbox and analytics. Each network is built on its official API and is being verified with live accounts.

social.featuresTitleDim: With your team and your approvals.

f1.d: Write once and adjust the text per network, with live previews, character counters and checks for photo size, ratio and video length.

f2.d: Month and week views, drag a post to reschedule it, recurring queue times per account and best-time suggestions from your own engagement.

f3.d: Members who need approval send their posts to an admin, who approves or rejects them with a comment. Everyone gets notified.

f4.d: Comments, mentions and direct messages where each network allows it. Reply, assign and mark done.

f5.d: Impressions, reach, engagement and clicks per post, followers per account and a CSV export.

f6.d: You connect your own developer apps, tokens are stored encrypted and each member only posts to the accounts you give them.

s1.d: An admin connects the company pages and profiles and chooses who posts to each one.

s2.d: Write the posts, fill the queue and send them for approval if needed.

s3.d: Reply from the inbox and check which posts worked.

compare.note: Hootsuite Standard is from $99 per user per month billed annually, per Hootsuite's plans page (October 29, 2026); Professional is from $199. A team of ten on Standard pays $11,880 a year. Social on your server costs $0; each network may charge for its own API (for example X).

f1.a: Facebook pages, Instagram business accounts, LinkedIn profiles and company pages, X, TikTok, YouTube, Threads and Bluesky. Bluesky connects with an app password; the rest need a developer app created by whoever runs the server. We are still verifying each network with live accounts.

f2.q: Do I need to create developer apps?
f2.a: Yes, on your own server. Each network asks for its own app (Meta, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, Google and Threads) and some, like Meta and LinkedIn, review it before you can post to company pages. The docs list every step and variable.

f3.q: What does the inbox include?
f3.a: Comments and messages on Facebook and Instagram, comments on LinkedIn, YouTube and Threads, replies and mentions on Bluesky, and mentions on X if your X API plan includes reading them. TikTok does not offer comments through its public API.

f4.q: Can someone post only after approval?
f4.a: Yes. Mark a member as needing approval and their posts wait for an admin, who approves or rejects them with a comment.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Hootsuite?
f5.a: Social listening, paid ads, employee advocacy, Pinterest, video on X and an AI writer inside the composer (the suite assistant can draft posts), among others. The parity table lists it row by row.

cta.title2: Tell us what you are missing.
cta.sub: Connect your accounts and vote on the public board for what we should do next.

meta.title: Hiring: open-source applicant tracking with a careers page
meta.description: Jobs from templates, a careers page with Google for Jobs data, a candidate pipeline, scorecards, interviews scheduled with Cal and offers your candidates accept online. An open-source alternative to Workable.

hero.sub: Publish jobs on your own careers page, move candidates through a kanban, collect scorecards from your interviewers and send offers, with candidate data visible only to each job's hiring team.

f1.d: Jobs from templates with department, location, remote or hybrid, employment type and an optional salary range. A careers page with your logo and color, JobPosting structured data and a sitemap.

f2.d: Resume upload checked by its bytes, custom questions, knock-out questions that flag answers for review, a consent checkbox and protection against bots and floods.

f3.d: A kanban per job with drag between stages, a list with filters, tags, sources with UTM, duplicate detection by email and a timeline with every email, note, move and score.

f4.d: Criteria per stage rated by each interviewer. Interviewers only see the candidates they evaluate and cannot see other scores for a stage until they submit their own. Recruiters and hiring managers see every scorecard. Reminders when feedback is late.

f5.d: Candidates pick a time when every interviewer is free, through Cal. Offer letters from a template, approved by the hiring manager and accepted by the candidate with a typed name.

f6.d: Candidate data only for the hiring team of each job and admins, also in search, the assistant and the API. Retention deletes old candidates and a link lets them delete their own data. AI only assists.

s1.d: Start from a template, set the hiring team and the stages with their scorecards.

s2.d: Share /careers/your-company or a short link with UTM.

s3.d: Move candidates, collect scorecards, schedule interviews and send the offer.

compare.per: priced by company size, monthly or yearly
compare.note: Workable sells plans that grow with the size of your company, plus paid add-ons. We could not verify the current prices, so check workable.com/pricing. Hiring on your server costs $0 plus your database and email sending.

f1.a: No. It can read a resume to fill fields and write a neutral summary. It never decides on a candidate; a person moves and rejects them.

f2.q: Who sees a candidate?
f2.a: The recruiters and hiring managers of the job they applied to, the interviewers asked to evaluate them, and the workspace admins. Nobody else, including in Cmd+K, the assistant and the API.

f3.q: Can candidates schedule their own interview?

f4.q: Is there electronic signature for offers?
f4.a: Not yet. The candidate accepts by typing their full name; Hiring stores the date, IP, browser and a hash of the letter.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Workable?
f5.a: Job board multiposting, a sourcing database, video interviews, assessments, SMS, e-signature and an HRIS. The parity table above has the full list.

cta.sub: Open Hiring, create your first job and publish your careers page.

meta.title: Books: open-source invoicing and accounting, a Xero alternative
meta.description: Invoices with taxes per line, online payment with Stripe or Mercado Pago, bills, expenses, bank reconciliation and double-entry accounting for small businesses in Latin America. An open-source alternative to Xero and QuickBooks.

hero.sub: Invoice in your currency with VAT per line, get paid online, load your bills and receipts, import your bank statement and reconcile it. Every document posts its own double-entry journal.

f1.d: Line items with VAT per line, discounts and due dates. Send by email with a link to view it online and pay with Stripe or Mercado Pago. Reminders go out on their own.

f2.d: Chart of accounts and taxes for Argentina and Mexico, letters A, B and C per point of sale, CUIT, RFC, CNPJ and CPF checked by their digits, and any currency with your exchange rate.

f3.d: Supplier bills with due dates, receipts that AI can read for you, purchase orders and receiving that raises stock. An item linked to Shop uses the store inventory.

f4.d: Import CSV or OFX statements and match each line with an invoice or bill from the suggestions, or turn it into an expense. There is no live bank connection yet.

f5.d: Every invoice, bill, payment and expense posts a balanced journal. Posted entries are never edited: you fix them with a credit note or a reversal, and a lock date closes the period.

f6.d: Profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, aged receivables and payables and the VAT sales and purchases books, exportable as CSV.

s1.d: Argentina, Mexico or generic: the chart of accounts, taxes and currency come ready.

s2.d: Paste your Stripe or Mercado Pago keys so customers can pay from the invoice.

s3.d: Create a customer, send the first invoice and watch it post to the ledger when it is paid.

compare.note: Xero plans are on xero.com/pricing. Books costs $0 on your server; Stripe and Mercado Pago charge their usual fees on each payment.

f1.q: Does it issue electronic invoices to ARCA (AFIP) or the SAT?
f1.a: Not yet. Books has the hook for a fiscal provider (ARCA, SAT CFDI through a PAC, or Invopop) and a test provider, but the real connectors are not built. You need your own certificates and provider account; the docs list what each one asks for.

f2.q: Does it connect to my bank?
f2.a: No. There are no live bank feeds. You download the statement from your bank as CSV or OFX and import it; Books skips lines it already has.

f3.q: Can my accountant use it?
f3.a: Yes. Give them the accountant role. Salespeople can have the sales role (invoices only) and partners the viewer role (reports).

f4.q: Can I correct an invoice after sending it?
f4.a: Not by editing it. A sent invoice keeps its amounts; you issue a credit note or void it, and the journal shows both entries.
